variant.stem_override: A 32-year-old man with a 3-year history of systemic lupus erythematosus (previously managed with hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisone) presents with 4 weeks of progressive lower-extremity edema and dark urine. Vital signs: BP 158/96 mmHg, HR 84 bpm. Labs: serum creatinine 1.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9), 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g, urinalysis with microscopic hematuria and red-cell casts; anti-dsDNA antibody 480 IU/mL (markedly elevated); C3 48 mg/dL and C4 6 mg/dL (markedly low). Renal biopsy demonstrates ISN/RPS Class IV (diffuse proliferative) lupus nephritis with NIH activity index 8/24 and chronicity index 1/12 (low chronicity). He is not pregnant, has no contraindications to standard immunosuppression, and is not planning a pregnancy in the next 12 months.
